title: Bupropion and naltrexone in methamphetamine use disorder

claims.statement: In adults with moderate or severe methamphetamine use disorder (403 randomized at eight US sites), extended-release injectable naltrexone plus oral bupropion produced a urine-verified response (at least 3 of 4 negative samples at the end of each 6-week stage) in 13.6% versus 2.5% on placebo, weighted across two stages: a difference of 11.1 percentage points (two-sided 95% CI about 6.2 to 16.0; number needed to treat 9). Nausea and vomiting were more frequent on treatment; serious adverse events were similar.
claims.magnitude: Weighted response 13.6% vs 2.5%; difference 11.1 percentage points (SE 2.5; editors' two-sided 95% CI 6.2–16.0); NNT 9. Stage 1: 16.5% vs 3.4%; stage 2: 11.4% vs 1.8%.
